Namespace: [Ankus](/api/ankus/)

Assembly: `Ankus.Runtime.dll`

Manages PostgreSQL's replication origins, which record how far a subscriber has applied each source's changes and
mark the commits it makes on that source's behalf.

```csharp
public static class PgReplicationOrigin
```

A worker that applies one source's changes sets up a session origin, then, in each transaction, records the
source's commit position and time before committing. PostgreSQL stores that position with the commit, so the
origin's progress survives a crash, and logical decoding can filter changes by the origin that made them. An
origin's numeric ID is what [CommitOrigin](/api/ankus.pgfoundrow/#member-808e760f6c408127) reports. Each operation makes the checks its
<code>pg_replication_origin_*</code> SQL function makes, except privileges: an extension decides who may call the functions
that use these operations. Creating, finding, dropping and advancing origins read or change the catalog, so they
need a transaction.

Inheritance: [object](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.object)

### Advance(ushort, PgLsn, PgLsn, bool, bool)

Moves an origin's progress, as <code>pg_replication_origin_advance</code> does.

```csharp
public static void Advance(ushort origin, PgLsn remoteCommit, PgLsn localCommit = default, bool goBackward = false, bool walLog = true)
```

Parameters:

`origin` — [ushort](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.uint16)

The origin's ID.

`remoteCommit` — [PgLsn](/api/ankus.pglsn/)

The source commit position the origin has applied.

`localCommit` — [PgLsn](/api/ankus.pglsn/)

The local commit that applied it, or [Invalid](/api/ankus.pglsn/#member-50847d69704f19f0).

`goBackward` — [bool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.boolean)

Whether the progress may move to an earlier position.

`walLog` — [bool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.boolean)

Whether to write the change to the write-ahead log so it survives a crash.

Exceptions:

- [PgException](/api/ankus.pgexception/): The origin does not exist, or there is no transaction.

Without <code class="paramref">goBackward</code>, an earlier position leaves the progress where it is. The SQL function
always allows moving backward.

```csharp
public static ushort Create(string name)
```

Parameters:

`name` — [string](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.string)

Returns: [ushort](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.uint16)

The new origin's ID.

Exceptions:

- [PgException](/api/ankus.pgexception/): An origin has the name, the name is reserved, or there is no transaction.

Names starting with <code>pg_</code> are reserved, and from PostgreSQL 16 so are <code>any</code> and <code>none</code>.

<a id="member-7e78734f266377f2"></a>

### SetTransactionOrigin(PgLsn, PgTimestampTz?)

Records the source's commit position and time for the current transaction, which PostgreSQL stores with its
commit and uses to advance the session origin's progress.

```csharp
public static void SetTransactionOrigin(PgLsn remoteCommit, PgTimestampTz? commitTime)
```

Parameters:

`remoteCommit` — [PgLsn](/api/ankus.pglsn/)

The position of the source's commit.

`commitTime` — <code>PgTimestampTz?</code>

The time the source committed, or null to record the local commit time.

Exceptions:

- [PgException](/api/ankus.pgexception/): The session has no origin, or there is no transaction.

PostgreSQL records the time as the commit timestamp in place of the local time. It keeps both values for the
session's later commits until they are set again or the session is reset, so an apply worker sets them in every
transaction it applies. PostgreSQL treats a time of zero, the start of 2000 UTC, as no time.
